items.title: SIU investigates after man found dead at University of Toronto Mississauga campus, shelter-in-place lifted
items.summary: The university issued the shelter-in-place alert after reports of an armed individual at the campus late Monday night. Police investigate at the McLuhan Court Residence at Dundas Street West and Mississauga Road on the University of Toronto Mississauga campus. The province’s police watchdog has invoked its mandate after a 19-year-old man was found dead following reports of gunshots and an armed individual at the University of Toronto’s Mississauga campus on Monday night, authorities said. The university says the overnight incident has “been resolved” and there is no threat to public safety. The University of Toronto issued a shelter-in-place order Monday night for its Mississauga campus after reports of gunshots. , Peel police responded to reports of an armed individual inside the McLuhan Court Residence at Dundas Street West and Mississauga Road. After officers arrived on scene, the suspect fired a gun from within a unit, police said in a statement Tuesday morning. Officers then moved to evacuate the building and the surrounding area.

A 19-year-old man wanted by Peel police in connection with an alleged assault in Brampton on Monday has died from a self-inflicted gunshot at the University of Toronto Mississauga, says the Special Investigations Unit. According to the SIU, Peel police received a 911 call during the afternoon of Nov. 2 after a man allegedly assaulted a woman in Brampton. m. At some point, said the SIU, “a gunshot was heard” and the suspect was later found inside the residence with a self-inflicted bullet wound. He died on Tuesday morning, added the SIU.

items.title: Classes cancelled as SIU investigates death at U of T Mississauga
items.summary: The University of Toronto cancelled classes at its Mississauga campus Tuesday after a 19-year-old man was found dead in a student residence following a police response Monday night. Ontario’s police watchdog is investigating the circumstances because Peel Regional Police officers were at the scene when the man died. The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) said Peel police received reports that a man had assaulted a woman in Brampton. m. at a student residence near Dundas Street West and Mississauga Road. The university issued a shelter-in-place order for students near McLuhan Court, a residence complex housing hundreds of first-year students, while police responded. “A gunshot was heard and the man was found inside with a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The man was pronounced deceased early this morning,” the SIU said. ” The university said it cancelled classes out of compassion for more than 2,000 students living in residence and others affected by the incident. The shelter-in-place order was also lifted. “Employees who were likewise required to shelter in place on campus last night will also take the time they need for their wellbeing,” the school said in a notice.

items.title: New Lego Store Set to Open at Square One This Friday, Completing GTA Trifecta
items.summary: The Lego Group says its new store at Mississauga's Square One Shopping Centre opens Friday, Nov. 6. According to the company, the roughly 2,970-square-foot store sits on the second floor in Unit 2-212, between La Vie en Rose and Indochino. The Lego Group said the Square One location completes a trio of new Lego stores opened across the Greater Toronto Area this fall. A Lego store opened at Markham's CF Markville in September, followed by another at Toronto's CF Eaton Centre in October. The company confirmed the Square One store would open to shoppers Friday morning, marking the third Lego-branded retail location to open in the GTA within about two months.

items.title: Peel Police Respond to Dangerous Weapons Call at UTM Residence, Triggering Overnight Shelter-in-Place
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say they responded to a dangerous weapons call at a University of Toronto Mississauga residence Monday night, prompting the school to order students to shelter in place. According to the university, the alert covered the McLuhan Court residence at 3330 Residence Road, which houses hundreds of first-year students. Police said the situation was isolated and contained to a single residential unit, with no injuries reported. The force said the immediate area was evacuated and asked the public to stay away while officers investigated overnight. Police confirmed there was no threat to public safety, though officers remained on the scene through the night. By Tuesday morning, both the university and police said the shelter-in-place order had been fully lifted and the incident resolved. Police have not released further details about the nature of the weapons call.

items.title: Peel Police Impound Multiple Vehicles After Halloween Weekend Blitz at Mississauga and Brampton Plazas
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say its Safer Roads Team targeted vehicle gatherings at Trinity Common Plaza in Brampton and Derry Financial Plaza in Mississauga over the Halloween weekend. According to police, officers impounded several vehicles for two weeks and handed drivers 30-day licence suspensions as part of the enforcement. The force said photos from the operation show Halloween-themed vehicles, including one covered in fake blood and another wrapped in caution tape, loaded onto flatbed trailers. Police said the crackdown follows years of complaints from residents about loud car rallies and street racing at plazas across Peel, including nearly 20,000 traffic charges laid across Mississauga and Brampton in the first half of 2024. Mississauga's Ridgeway Plaza and Brampton's Trinity Common Mall have both repeatedly drawn these gatherings, prompting Brampton to pass bylaws with fines of $800 to $2,000 for the nuisance. Police said the Safer Roads Team plans to keep up enforcement at both locations.

items.title: Mississauga Library Hosts Its Annual Comic and Gaming Expo This Weekend at the Central Library
items.summary: The Mississauga Library says its annual Comic Expo, known as MCX, returns Nov. 6 and 7 at the Hazel McCallion Central Library on Burnhamthorpe Road. According to organizers, the free, all-ages event is one of the library's most popular annual draws and celebrates comics, games, manga and fandom. The library said visitors can take part in a cosplay red carpet, pose at a green-screen photo booth and browse a trading post for collectibles. Organizers added that the schedule includes workshops and panels on topics like gag comics and miniature building, along with free-play video games and trivia contests. The event comes just days after Halloween, giving costume fans another reason to keep their outfits ready. Admission remains free throughout the weekend, the library said.

items.title: Dangerous driving charges laid in Mississauga crash that killed father, daughter
items.summary: A Mississauga man faces two charges of dangerous driving causing death in a devastating Highway 401 crash this past summer that killed a father and daughter as they were leaving town on vacation. m. in the eastbound express lanes of the busy highway near Dixie Road in Mississauga. Ralph Crane, 80, and his daughter, Sheri-Lynn Crane-Gormley, 53, both of Cambridge, died when the Honda CR-V in which they were passengers was struck from behind by a Mercedes SUV as traffic slowed down during rush-hour conditions. OPP have not released their names, but the two people killed, who were pronounced dead at the scene, were identified earlier in an obituary published by Corbett Funeral Home. Police did say at the time, though, that four people were inside the vehicle when it was rear-ended. “The two other family member occupants were transported to hospital, one with serious injuries and the other with non-life-threatening injuries,” OPP said in a news release on Monday. The driver of the other vehicle, who was the lone occupant, was transported to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police added. L.
